newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Foster's, Molson in buyback talks.
newsitem.headline: Foster's, Molson in buyback talks.

text.p: Canada's Molson Cos Ltd and Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd are said to be in talks to buy 20 percent of Molson Breweries from U.S. brewer Miller.
A document prepared recently for the sale of a major parcel of Foster's shares reveal that talks with Miller, a unit of Philip Morris Cos Inc, are at an "advanced stage".
Foster's and Molson Cos each sold 10 percent of Molson Breweries, Canada's largest brewer, to Miller in 1993. The deal left Foster's and Molson Cos each with a 40 percent stake.
The sale proved later to be a major and costly headache for Molson Breweries and its shareholders.
The sale was found to breach the conditions of a licencing agreement with Miller's U.S. rival, Adolph Coors Co.
Settlement of the dispute cost Molson Breweries C$100 million.

"Foster's and TMLC (Molson Cos) are in discussions with Miller regarding a transaction involving a pro-rata repurchase of Miller's 20 percent interest in Molson," said the document, released by Foster's shareholder, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd.
"These discussions have reached an advanced stage although certain issues remain outstanding. Should the transaction be consummated, Foster's would be required to outlay significant funds."
The document gave no more details and Foster's declined to comment on Tuesday.
BHP released the document after announcing this month it would sell its 37 percent stake in Foster's.
Most of the shares were sold immediately to institutions, but some have been set aside for an offer to BHP shareholders.
